title: Tenant burst reservation and wildcard routing — notes
content:
Goal: sketch an API + runtime shape for tenant-level burst reservations and a wildcard routing mode that lets lightweight clients tag requests for opportunistic capacity without forcing tenant-wide capacity changes.

Context / why:
- Product ask: marketing + some PLG users want temporary burst capacity guarantees for 1–3 minute windows during spikes (e.g., demo, launch, inbound traffic surge).
- We already have reserved capacity (Dedicated) and on-demand hosted. Reserved is coarse (monthly/annum) and on-demand has cold-start and throttling at high concurrency. Need a mid-tier primitive: short-lived burst reservations that can be cheaply hedged by routing and soft-fallbacks.
- This is a personal sketch to iterate with SRE + Serving runtime. Not final.

Requirements (informal):
- API: tenants (or API keys) can request a burst reservation with: desired qps, max tokens/s, duration (<= 5 minutes), priority tag, optional fallback policy (downgrade to cheaper model).
- Admission: controller should accept, partially accept, or queue. Partial accept = grant fraction of requested qps or timesliced allocations.
- Billing: usage-based for granted tokens/time; early-cancel refunds pro-rated.
- Observability: per-burst metrics (granted_qps, used_qps, tail_latency_p99, fallback_count).
- Isolation: bursts should not starve long-lived reserved tenants; enforce fair share and emergency preemption triggers.

High-level flow:
1) Client POST /v1/bursts with payload (see API shape below).
2) Admission controller checks cluster headroom, tenant limits, recent burst history, and policy rules.
3) If accepted, controller returns a burst_id and per-shard routing hints.
4) Client annotates subsequent calls with header X-Burst-ID: <id> or ?burst_id= param.
5) Ingress router uses burst routing rules to route eligible requests to burst pool nodes or to preferred model variants.
6) Bursts are enforced by token buckets on the serving side; prefix caching and KV reuse allowed.
7) At end, controller emits summary event and billing record.

API shape (sketch):
POST /v1/bursts\Body (json):
{
  "tenant_id": "t-abc123",
  "requested_qps": 120,
  "max_tokens_per_minute": 200000,
  "duration_seconds": 180,
  "priority": "elevated",    // low | normal | elevated
  "fallback_policy": "fallback-to-small-model:embedding-lite-v2", // optional
  "routing_constraints": {"region": "us-west1", "avoid_nodes": ["node-4"]},
  "client_context": {"reason": "launch-demo"}
}

Response (200/202/409):
{
  "burst_id": "b-20241107-01",
  "granted_qps": 80,
  "granted_tokens_per_minute": 100000,
  "start_ts": "2024-11-07T15:01:27Z",
  "end_ts": "2024-11-07T15:04:27Z",
  "status": "partial_accept"
}

Edge cases:
- If controller returns partial accept we provide per-request rejection/backoff headers: X-Burst-Accept: partial or X-Burst-Token-Available: 0/1.
- If clients try to game the API (open many bursts), rate limit by tenant and require billing commitment above N concurrent bursts.

Wildcard routing mode (idea):
- Lightweight clients (web widgets, SDKs) can opt-in to `routing_hint: "wildcard-burst"` on normal requests instead of opening an explicit burst.
- Router probabilistically routes a fraction of those requests into burst pool when capacity available. Fraction controlled by tenant-level wildcard_fraction config and global policy.
- Use-case: demo page with low overhead; if capacity available occasionally get low latency.
- Probabilistic routing avoids strong admission flow and is cheap for clients.

Config sketch (YAML-ish, per-tenant):
tenant_config:
  tenant_id: t-abc123
  burst_quota:
    max_concurrent_bursts: 2
    max_total_seconds_per_day: 1200
    min_grant_qps: 10
  wildcard:
    enabled: true
    global_fraction: 0.02
    tenant_fraction_override: 0.1
  fallback_rules:
    - when: "tokens_exhausted"
      action: "route_to: small-model-v2"
    - when: "latency_p99 > 500ms"
      action: "throttle: 50%"

Runtime admission heuristics (notes to self):
- Admission window should look at 30s rolling headroom and a 5m smoothed demand estimate.
- Allow partial grants on each shard using linear allocation: grant_i = min(request_i, shard_headroom * share_factor).
- Preemption: if a reserved tenant needs capacity, bursts older than "grace_period" (e.g., 30s) can be preempted. Preemption must trigger graceful fallback.

Serving-side enforcement:
- Attach burst_id to request context; token bucket keyed by (burst_id, tenant_id).
- When routing_hint == wildcard-burst: treat as best-effort and check shard spare capacity metric.
- Track KV cache affinity: prefer routing burst requests to nodes that already have warm KV state for the tenant’s common prefixes.

Observability & instrumentation:
- Expose /metrics counters: burst_granted_total{tenant,priority}, burst_used_tokens_total, burst_preempted_total, burst_fallbacks_total.
- Add tracing span: burst.admission -> burst.routing -> serving.execute
- Emit events to billing pipeline: burst_start, burst_update (used tokens), burst_end, burst_cancel.

Failure modes and mitigations: 
- Overcommit: if controller overgrants, tails spike. Mitigate by conservative defaults and emergency circuit-breaker that reduces wildcard_fraction globally.
- Gaming: client opens many small bursts to circumvent reserved capacity. Mitigate: cost floor for bursts and per-tenant concurrent limits.
- KV churn: bursts hitting different nodes cause cache evictions. Mitigate: routing affinity hints, small TTL on noncritical cached prefixes.

Questions / open design points:
- Billing model: flat minimum per burst? or purely usage? likely need small minimum to discourage abuse. What's the minimum that sales is OK with? (ask @Lena)
- Should wildcard routing be opt-in at tenant-level or opt-in at SDK-level? SDK opt-in easier to push, tenant opt-in safer.
- How to express multi-tenant fairness with mix of reserved + bursts + wildcard best-effort? Do we use weighted fair share across classes or strict precedence?
- Preemption policy: should we preempt lowest-priority bursts first, or use oldest-first? (pref: combine priority then age)

Simulation notes (quick rough sim):
- Cluster capacity: 2000 qps spare for bursts. 50 tenants, avg requested burst qps=200 -> naive full accept would overcommit.
- If we limit granted_fraction to 0.4 of request we stay within capacity in 95% of simulated workloads.
- Wildcard_fraction global default 0.02 yields ~40 qps in the above cluster -> helps small demo bursts with minimal impact.

Rollout plan (alpha -> beta):
- Alpha (internal): implement controller + ingress routing flags; limit to internal tenants; no billing; telemetry only; run for 2 weeks.
- Beta (select customers): opt-in via tenant_config; enable billing with small fee; monitor interference signals for 1 month.
- GA: public SDK flag + console UI to create bursts; integration with billing and fraud-detection.

TODOs (next actions):
- [ ] Spike: lightweight admission controller prototype (Samir)
- [ ] Prototype ingress hint plumbing (Lena)
- [ ] Mock billing event schema (me)
- [ ] Draft UX for console: create burst modal and realtime usage bar (product)
- [ ] Quick sim harness to test overcommit thresholds (SRE)

Notes to self: keep API minimal for alpha. Focus on safety (limits, defaults) more than features. Expect follow-up iterations with SRE on preemption semantics.

References / links to look up while iterating:
- existing admission-control heuristics: GH PR #2998 (admission-control refactor)
- billing event schema: docs/billing/events.md (internal)
- handoff: sync with @Lena on routing-affinity primitives

Rough ascii diagram (Ingress -> Controller -> Serving):

Client --POST /v1/bursts--> AdmissionController ---allocates---> BurstPool
         |                          |                         |
         |-- subsequent requests --(X-Burst-ID header)--------> Ingress Router --routes--> BurstServingNodes (token bucket per burst)
                                                                                          |-> FallbackServingNodes (on fallback)

End.
